judgments.reasoning_cat1: An exhaustive sweep of every kind of liability owing to Lender, plus Bank Product Obligations; broad but drafted to remove doubt rather than create it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Obligations" is the numerator of the Senior Leverage Ratio, the measure in Sections 3.6, 3.7 and 9.1(a), and its inclusion of contingent Bank Product Obligations makes the 0.9% ratio in Section 7.16(b) harder still to satisfy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the Offering Circular "collectively" to include the operating agreement, subscription agreements and "related agreements and instruments," an open-ended tail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.3's warranty that the Offering Circular complies with all securities laws, and Section 6.3(d)(iii)'s delivery duty, both turn on this elastic scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines a certificate by reference to a form Lender submits, with responses that must satisfy Lender; definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(b)(vi) requires its delivery and it is a Loan Document, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4 creates the term as stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.1(d) creates the term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable (from the perspective of a secured asset-based lender) business judgment" is a deliberately soft standard whose content is contestable in every application.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The agreement elsewhere uses "sole discretion" (Borrower's Required Procedures, Section 3.1(k)) and "reasonable discretion" (Approved Title Insurance Company), so three different discretion standards coexist and must be sorted out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of seven permitted dispositions closing with unqualified categories, and clause (e) mis-states the price floor as "not less than eighty (80%) of the unpaid balance" — the word "percent" is missing, so the numeral and the parenthetical do not agree. The enumerated-exception structure also raises an expressio unius question about anything not listed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This definition is the sole gateway through Section 4.1's flat ban on disposing of Collateral, Section 7.3(c) and Section 7.4, and it interlocks with Section 4.9(b)'s lien release on sale and Section 2.6(a)(iii)'s routing of sale proceeds; whether a given sale of Notes Receivable was permitted turns on reconciling all four.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of four named individuals; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Change of Control definition requires Permitted Holders to own 100% of Manager and Servicer, yet the Executive Officer and Validity Agreement Party lists include a fifth person, a mismatch worth noting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Six enumerated categories, each reasonably bounded; clause (d) ("commercial loans evidenced by a Note Receivable made in the ordinary course") is the operative one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Section 7.12's prohibition and the Permitted Reorganization carve-out coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (c) reads "so long as such Liens for Approved Debt or subordinated to the Liens held by Lender" — "or" plainly should be "are," and the error goes to whether subordination is a condition of the permission.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule P-1 lists the Fremont Bank lien and the future Approved Debt liens, and Section 7.2 permits only Permitted Liens, so the garbled condition matters to the priority scheme with Section 5.9(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three cumulative conditions, one of which turns on Lender being "satisfied"; workable but discretionary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Sections 6.7, 6.11 and Permitted Liens clauses (b) and (f).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A hard dollar cap on purchase money debt; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1(c) permits it and Permitted Liens clause (e) secures it, although clause (e) refers to "Purchase Money Indebtedness" and then to "Permitted Purchase Money Indebtedness," a loose usage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permitted transaction is defined by reference to "the written description provided to Lender by Borrowers prior to the Closing Date," an extrinsic document, with conformity measured only "in all material respects."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Reorganization is the carve-out from Sections 7.3(a),(b), 7.6, 7.12 and the source of Approved Debt and Subordinated Notes, so its indeterminate content controls much of the negative-covenant package.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad enumeration of entity types ending with "or other organizations, irrespective of whether they are legal entities"; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear description of forecast financial statements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No operative provision in the delivered text actually requires Projections, leaving this an orphan definition — untidy but harmless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Twenty-day acquisition window and stated purpose make it definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with Permitted Purchase Money Indebtedness and Permitted Liens clause (e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by the manner of acquisition following default; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Dispositions clause (g) permits its sale and Permitted Investments clause (f) permits holding it, consistently; it is also reported on the Borrowing Base Certificate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard real property definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.4(c), 5.1 and the Lien definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: UCC-style definition of a record; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.4's rule that any writing requirement is satisfied by a Record, and that a Record is a warranty of accuracy, is a strong consequence but coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Five enumerated categories closing with "any other actions ... authorized by Environmental Laws," a bounded catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.13 and 11.3(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by Federal Reserve regulation with a zero default; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds the LIBOR Rate formula consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (d) is circular — a payment is a Restricted Payment only "to the extent such action would cause an Event of Default to occur hereunder" — and clause (e) sweeps in any payment to a holder of Stock "not expressly authorized in this Agreement."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.10 then permits Tax Distributions, returns of capital "required or permitted by Fund's Governing Documents" and Subordinated Debt payments, so the prohibition and its exceptions have to be reconciled; the definition's own reference back to Events of Default compounds it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple measure of outstanding Advances.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in Section 2.1(c)'s caps and the Unused Line Fee; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Institutional reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the Stock definition and Section 6.3(d); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: UCC-referential one-liner.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.7 and 5.18.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is defined as a "ratio" of Obligations to Tangible Net Worth, yet Section 7.16(b) and Schedule 3 express it as a percentage, so the unit of measurement is not fixed by the definition itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Section 7.16(b)'s 0.9% ceiling, the $600,000,000 Tangible Net Worth floor and the $50,000,000 Maximum Revolver Amount, the covenant would be breached by ordinary borrowing — a genuine internal incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a single corporation; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Bar-K is excluded from "Subsidiary" yet the Change of Control definition polices its ownership and Section 8.15 polices the Servicing Agreement, a deliberate but slightly awkward treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies an agreement "between Borrower, Servicer and Lender" (singular Borrower) relating to servicing; short and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a Loan Document, a Section 3.1(b)(iv) condition, and the reference point for Sections 4.8, 8.15 and 9.1(e)/(o); nothing contradicts it, though its terms are extrinsic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines who may disburse loan proceeds, with a parenthetical list and a closing-protection-letter requirement; the parenthesis is unclosed in the text but the sense is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.18 requires initial disbursements through a Settlement Agent by reference to "Section 3.3(z)," a subsection that does not exist, which undercuts the mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The solvency test is truncated to a single balance-sheet comparison ("at fair valuations, the sum of such Person's assets is greater than all of such Person's debts"), omitting the usual capital-adequacy and ability-to-pay limbs, so what "Solvent" means is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.12(a) warrants solvency and Section 5.12(b) disclaims fraudulent intent, and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (q) turns on makers being Solvent, so the truncated test carries weight across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad equity definition "regardless of how designated"; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applied to LLC membership interests in Sections 5.8, 7.8 and the Change of Control definition without difficulty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (a) requires "unsecured Indebtedness" while clause (b) admits Approved Debt, which the deal contemplates being secured; the internal pairing is uneasy on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Subordinated Note definition describes notes "secured by the assets of Fund," and Permitted Liens clause (c) permits liens for Approved Debt, so the "unsecured" requirement in clause (a) has to be confined to non-Approved Debt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap is measured against members' capital accounts "taking into account, in Manager's discretion, the realized and unrealized gains, losses and items of income," which makes the ceiling depend on the borrower's own discretionary accounting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Subordinated Debt clause (a)'s "unsecured" requirement and Section 7.7(b)'s payment restrictions; the discretionary sizing is the sort of term a creditor would later attack.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two-limb definition keyed to who signs; "form and substance satisfactory to Lender" is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Approved Debt, Subordinated Debt and Section 7.10(b) machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso excludes from "Subsidiary" any entity formed after the Closing Date that is not funded with a Borrower's assets, plus any New Fund and Bar-K, so an entity can be controlled yet not a Subsidiary — a significant and contestable carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.13's first sentence forbids forming any Subsidiary without consent while this definition contemplates new entities being formed and simply not counted, and Schedule 5.7(a)/5.8 state there are none.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: UCC-derived and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Borrower Collateral clause (j).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An arithmetic formula, but it adds Subordinated Debt to members' equity, so debt counts as net worth — clear as drafted, if commercially unusual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.16(a) requires $600,000,000 and Section 7.16(b) divides Obligations by this figure; because Approved Debt issued in the reorganization would be added back, the covenant's bite depends on that interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The measure is taxes "payable by such holders ... attributable to the taxable income or gain of such Borrower," but the sentence began with distributions by "Fund or Manager," so the antecedent of "such Borrower" is imprecise, and the highest-marginal-rate assumption is a proxy rather than actual tax.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.10(a)(i) permits Tax Distributions notwithstanding the Restricted Payments ban, so the size of this permitted leakage matters to the Lender's covenant package.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.5 defines Taxes as stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two objective triggers, one of which (aggregate Notes Receivable below $500,000,000) is a bright line; "has occurred" is not paired with "and is continuing" here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(b) promises no reserves "unless a Triggering Event has occurred and is continuing," adding a continuation requirement absent from the definition, and the Bank Product Reserve appears to escape that limit altogether.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-evident.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular but conventional definition of a validity agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(b)(iii) requires delivery and Section 8.12 makes termination a default; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of five named individuals; definite despite OCR spelling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Executive Officer list and Section 8.12; the four-person Permitted Holders list is deliberately narrower.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.7 creates the term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a specific bank; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Base Rate and Bank Product Provider definitions depend on it, and Lender is an affiliate, which is consistent though it collapses roles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence deems "Borrower" in any financial covenant to mean Fund and its Subsidiaries consolidated "unless the context clearly requires otherwise" — an escape hatch that undoes the very rule it states.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.16(b) measures "all Obligations of Borrower" against Fund's Tangible Net Worth, and the Borrowers are jointly liable under Section 2.13, so whose obligations are counted is not settled by this rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Supplies a clean tie-breaker to Article 9 where the Code defines a term differently in different Articles.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with the "Code" definition and the many UCC-referential defined terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It legislates that "or" means "and/or" and that "including" is non-limiting, which resolves some ambiguities but manufactures others (every disjunctive list becomes conjunctive-capable).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Combined with Section 16.3's anti-construction-against-drafter rule and Section 16.2's headings clause, these interpretive directives govern how every catch-all in the instrument is read.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line incorporation clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B-2 is a placeholder ("form to be provided by Lender"), so incorporation by reference cannot supply its content for Sections 3.3(f) and 6.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear lesser-of formulation subject to the terms and conditions of the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The commitment must be read with Section 2.1(c)'s additional caps, Section 3.3's conditions and the Section 7.16(b) leverage ceiling, which as drafted would prevent full utilisation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause first gives Lender an open right to set reserves "as Lender in its Permitted Discretion shall deem necessary or appropriate," then flatly says Lender "agrees not to establish any such reserves unless a Triggering Event has occurred" — a right and its negation in the same paragraph, plus duplicative clauses (iii) and (iv) on valuation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Borrowing Base deducts both these reserves and the separately defined Bank Product Reserve, which is not obviously subject to the Triggering Event promise, and Section 10 lets Lender set further reserves on a borrower payment failure without any such limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence's cap — the unused commitment plus cash in Cash Management Accounts may not exceed unfunded commitments to makers of Notes Receivable — is densely drafted and its purpose is not self-evident from the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It layers a third limit on top of the Maximum Revolver Amount and Borrowing Base in Section 2.1(a), and interacts with Section 2.6's sweep of all cash to Lender's Account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple revolving-credit statement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1(a) and 3.4's term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short conditions-precedent reservation referring expressly to Section 3.3.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Section 3.3's own lead-in, which is redundant but harmonious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same-day noon deadline for a written request, with telephonic notice permitted "at Lender's election," and a statement that failure to confirm in writing does not affect validity; workable but the election mechanic is loosely expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.8 separately authorizes Lender to advance on instructions "from anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person," a materially looser standard than this section's request procedure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward funding mechanic naming the Designated Account or a Settlement Agent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.8 and 6.18's Settlement Agent disbursement requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise timing and funds requirements; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with Section 2.7's crediting rules, which use the same 1:00 p.m. cut-off.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eight-tier waterfall with defined triggers, plus its own definition of "paid in full"; long but carefully drafted and internally ordered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (iv) expressly anticipates conflicts with other Loan Documents and makes this section control, which is exactly the harmonising device a court would apply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines an Overadvance as any excess over "any of the limitations set forth in Section 2.1," which requires the reader to pick through three different caps in that section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Section 2.3(b)'s application priorities and to Section 2.3(b)(i)(D)'s no-Overadvance election, which cohere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two-rate formulation keyed to defined loan types; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Applicable Margin definition and Section 2.12's LIBOR mechanics.
